title: Ethiopian Lamb Curry
community: Urban Ethiopia — the Indian Ocean spice influence
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Lamb Curry — lamb slow-simmered with an Ethiopian-influenced curry sauce combining berbere, turmeric, cardamom, and coriander with tomato and onion. The cross-cultural dish of Ethiopia's urban kitchens — the curry that has absorbed the Ethiopian spice tradition completely.
longDesc: Ethiopian lamb curry reflects the country's gradual absorption of South Asian culinary influences through Somali and Djibouti traders — the familiar curry format applied to lamb but seasoned with berbere and mekelesha instead of garam masala.
steps: Cook onions until very golden — 12 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, all spices, and tomatoes. Cook 8 minutes.
Simmer covered 60—70 minutes until very tender.
chefTips: The berbere in a curry context gives it an unmistakably Ethiopian character.
Low and slow for the tenderness.
cookingScience: See ETH025 for lamb cooking science. The Ethiopian curry differs from South Asian curry in the absence of coconut milk or cream — producing a drier, more concentrated sauce.
culturalNote: Ethiopian lamb curry is the meeting of Ethiopian highland cooking with the Indian Ocean trade routes — a dish that belongs to no single food tradition but to the crossroads Ethiopia has always occupied.
